verses.1:1: What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we observed and our hands touched, concerning the Word of life—
verses.1:2: and the life was revealed, and we have seen and bear witness and proclaim to you the eternal life that was with the Father and was revealed to us—
verses.1:3: what we have seen and heard we proclaim to you as well, so that you also may have fellowship with us; and our fellowship is indeed with the Father and with His Son Jesus Christ.
verses.1:4: And we are writing these things so that our joy may be made complete.
verses.1:5: And this is the message that we have heard from Him and declare to you: that God is light, and there is no darkness in Him at all.
verses.1:6: If we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in the darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.
verses.1:7: But if we walk in the light as He Himself is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus, His Son, cleanses us from every sin.
verses.1:8: If we say that we have no sin, we lead ourselves astray, and the truth is not in us.
verses.1:9: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and righteous so that He will forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
verses.1:10: If we say that we have not sinned, we make Him out to be a liar, and His word is not in us.
verses.2:1: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you will not sin. And if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous One;
verses.2:2: and He Himself is the atonement for our sins, and not for ours alone, but also for the whole world.
verses.2:3: And by this we know that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments.
verses.2:4: The one who says, "I have come to know Him," and does not keep His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in that person.
verses.2:5: But whoever keeps His word, truly in that person the love of God has been brought to perfection. By this we know that we are in Him:
verses.2:6: the one who says he remains in Him ought himself to walk just as He walked.
verses.2:7: Beloved, I am not writing a new commandment to you, but an old commandment that you had from the beginning; the old commandment is the word that you heard.
verses.2:8: Yet again, I am writing a new commandment to you, which is true in Him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining.
verses.2:9: The one who says he is in the light while hating his brother is in the darkness until now.
verses.2:10: The one who loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no cause for stumbling in him.
verses.2:11: But the one who hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness blinded his eyes.
verses.2:12: I am writing to you, little children, because your sins have been forgiven on account of His name.
verses.2:13: I am writing to you, fathers, because you have come to know Him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have conquered the evil one.
verses.2:14: I wrote to you, children, because you have come to know the Father. I wrote to you, fathers, because you have come to know Him who is from the beginning. I wrote to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God remains in you, and you have conquered the evil one.
verses.2:15: Do not love the world nor the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him,
verses.2:16: because everything that is in the world—the desire of the flesh and the desire of the eyes and the boastfulness of life—is not from the Father, but is from the world.
verses.2:17: And the world is passing away, and so is its desire, but the one who does the will of God remains forever.
verses.2:18: Children, it is the last hour; and just as you heard that antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have arisen. From this we know that it is the last hour.
verses.2:19: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would have remained with us. Yet they went out so that it might be revealed that not all are of us.
verses.2:20: And you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you all know.
verses.2:21: I did not write to you because you do not know the truth, but because you do know it, and because no lie is from the truth.
verses.2:22: Who is the liar except the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, the one who denies the Father and the Son.
verses.2:23: Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father either; the one who confesses the Son has the Father as well.
verses.2:24: As for you, let what you heard from the beginning remain in you. If what you heard from the beginning remains in you, you too will remain in the Son and in the Father.
verses.2:25: And this is the promise that He Himself promised to us: eternal life.
verses.2:26: I wrote these things to you concerning those who are leading you astray.
verses.2:27: And as for you, the anointing that you received from Him remains in you, and you have no need for anyone to teach you; instead, as His anointing teaches you about all things—and is true and is no lie—even as it taught you, remain in Him.
verses.2:28: And now, little children, remain in Him, so that when He is revealed we may have confidence and not be put to shame before Him at His coming.
verses.2:29: If you know that He is righteous, you recognize that everyone who practices righteousness has also been born of Him.
verses.3:1: Look at what sort of love the Father has given us, that we might be called children of God—and so we are. Because of this the world does not know us, since it did not know Him.
verses.3:2: Beloved, now we are children of God, and it has not yet been revealed what we will be. We know that when He is revealed we will be like Him, because we will see Him just as He is.
verses.3:3: And everyone who has this hope in Him purifies himself, just as He is pure.
verses.3:4: Everyone who practices sin practices lawlessness as well, and sin is lawlessness.
verses.3:5: And you know that He was revealed to take away sins, and in Him there is no sin.
verses.3:6: Everyone who remains in Him does not sin; everyone who sins has neither seen Him nor come to know Him.
verses.3:7: Little children, let no one lead you astray: the one who practices righteousness is righteous, just as He is righteous.
verses.3:8: The one who practices sin is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was revealed: so that He might destroy the works of the devil.
verses.3:9: Everyone who has been born of God does not practice sin, because His seed remains in him; and he is not able to sin, because he has been born of God.
verses.3:10: By this the children of God and the children of the devil are evident: everyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is the one who does not love his brother.
verses.3:11: For this is the message that you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another,
verses.3:12: not like Cain, who was of the evil one and slaughtered his brother. And for what reason did he slaughter him? Because his own works were evil, whereas those of his brother were righteous.
verses.3:13: Do not be amazed, brothers, if the world hates you.
verses.3:14: We know that we have crossed over from death into life, because we love the brothers. The one who does not love remains in death.
verses.3:15: Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him.
verses.3:16: By this we have come to know love: that He laid down His life on our behalf; and we ought to lay down our lives on behalf of the brothers.
verses.3:17: But whoever has the world's means of living and sees his brother in need, and closes his compassion against him, how does the love of God remain in him?
verses.3:18: Little children, let us not love in word or with the tongue, but in deed and truth.
verses.3:19: By this we will know that we are of the truth and will reassure our hearts before Him,
verses.3:20: whenever our heart condemns us, because God is greater than our heart and knows all things.
verses.3:21: Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence before God,
verses.3:22: and whatever we ask we receive from Him, because we keep His commandments and do the things that are pleasing in His sight.
verses.3:23: And this is His commandment: that we believe in the name of His Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another, just as He gave us a commandment.
verses.3:24: And the one who keeps His commandments remains in Him, and He in him. And by this we know that He remains in us: by the Spirit whom He gave to us.
verses.4:1: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but put the spirits to the test to see whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
verses.4:2: By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ as having come in the flesh is from God,
verses.4:3: and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God; and this is the spirit of the antichrist, which you have heard is coming, and now it is already in the world.
verses.4:4: You are from God, little children, and you have conquered them, because greater is the One who is in you than the one who is in the world.
verses.4:5: They are from the world; because of this, they speak from the world, and the world listens to them.
verses.4:6: We are from God. The one who knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. From this we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of deception.
verses.4:7: Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God, and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
verses.4:8: The one who does not love has not come to know God, because God is love.
verses.4:9: By this the love of God was revealed among us: that God has sent His only Son into the world so that we might live through Him.
verses.4:10: In this is love: not that we have loved God, but that He Himself loved us and sent His Son as a propitiation for our sins.
verses.4:11: Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another.
verses.4:12: No one has seen God at any time; if we love one another, God remains in us, and His love is made complete in us.
verses.4:13: By this we know that we remain in Him and He in us, because He has given to us from His Spirit.
verses.4:14: And we ourselves have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son as Savior of the world.
verses.4:15: Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him, and he in God.
verses.4:16: And we have come to know and have believed the love that God has for us. God is love, and the one who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.
verses.4:17: By this, love has been made complete with us, so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment, because just as He is, so also are we in this world.
verses.4:18: There is no fear in love, but complete love drives out fear, because fear involves punishment, and the one who fears has not been made complete in love.
verses.4:19: We love, because He Himself loved us first.
verses.4:20: If anyone says, "I love God," and hates his brother, he is a liar; for the one who does not love his brother, whom he has seen, is not able to love God, whom he has not seen.
verses.4:21: And we have this commandment from Him: that the one who loves God must also love his brother.
verses.5:1: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the One who gave birth also loves the one born of Him.
verses.5:2: In this way we know that we love God's children: whenever we love God and keep His commandments.
verses.5:3: For the love of God is this: that we keep His commandments, and His commandments are not burdensome,
verses.5:4: because everything that has been born of God conquers the world. And this is the victory that has conquered the world: our faith.
verses.5:5: And who is the one who conquers the world except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?
verses.5:6: This is the One who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ—not with the water alone, but with the water and with the blood. And the Spirit is the One who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth.
verses.5:7: For there are three who testify,
verses.5:8: the Spirit and the water and the blood, and the three agree as one.
verses.5:9: If we accept the testimony of people, the testimony of God is greater, because this is the testimony of God: that He has testified concerning His Son.
verses.5:10: The one who believes in the Son of God has the testimony within himself; the one who does not believe God has made Him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has testified concerning His Son.
verses.5:11: And the testimony is this: that God gave to us eternal life, and this life is in His Son.
verses.5:12: The one who has the Son has the life; the one who does not have the Son of God does not have the life.
verses.5:13: I have written these things to you so that you may know that you have eternal life—to you who believe in the name of the Son of God.
verses.5:14: And this is the confidence that we have toward Him: that if we ask anything according to His will, He listens to us.
verses.5:15: And if we know that He listens to us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests that we have asked from Him.
verses.5:16: If anyone sees his brother committing a sin not leading to death, he will ask, and He will give him life—to those committing sin not leading to death. There is a sin leading to death; I am not saying that he should make a request concerning that.
verses.5:17: All wrongdoing is sin, and there is sin that does not lead to death.
verses.5:18: We know that everyone who has been born of God does not sin, but the One who was born of God keeps him, and the evil one does not touch him.
verses.5:19: We know that we are from God, and the entire world lies under the evil one.
verses.5:20: And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we know the True One; and we are in the True One, in His Son Jesus Christ. This One is the true God and eternal life.
verses.5:21: Little children, guard yourselves against idols.

notes.1:1: The neuter relative pronoun "What" (Greek ho) and the phrase "the Word of life" embrace both the gospel message proclaimed by the eyewitnesses and the personal Christ who embodies life.
notes.1:4: The Greek text reads "our joy" (hemon), whereas some manuscripts read "your joy" (hymon).
notes.2:2: The Greek noun hilasmos ("atonement") is variously rendered "propitiation" (turning away wrath) or "expiation" (wiping away guilt).
notes.2:14: The shift from present "I am writing" in vv. 12-13 to aorist "I wrote" in v. 14 is often understood either as an epistolary aorist written from the readers' standpoint or as looking back to the preceding section.
notes.2:20: The Greek text reads "you all know" (oidate pantes), while many later manuscripts read "you know all things" (oidate panta).
notes.2:27: The verb menete is identical in form for the imperative ("remain in Him") and the indicative ("you remain in Him"); the imperative matches the clear command in v. 28.
notes.3:2: Because the verb phanerothe ("is revealed") has no explicit subject, the clause can mean either "when He is revealed" (cf. 2:28) or "when it [what we will be] is revealed."
notes.3:6: The present-tense verbs "does not sin" and "sins" (and "to sin" in v. 9) are debated, being interpreted either as referring to habitual, ongoing sinning or as an absolute contrast between the realms of light and darkness.
notes.3:9: "His seed" (sperma autou) is variously interpreted as God's word, the Holy Spirit, or the divine life imparted in the new birth.
notes.3:20: The Greek has a syntactically difficult double hoti ("that/because"); taking the first as indefinite ho ti ean ("whenever" or "in whatever") followed by causal hoti ("because") is the most widely adopted reading.
notes.4:3: Early Greek manuscripts read simply 'does not confess Jesus'; later manuscripts expand this to match v. 2, while a few Latin and patristic witnesses read 'annuls' or 'dissolves' Jesus.
notes.4:9: The Greek adjective monogenes ('only') denotes a unique, one-of-a-kind son; 'among us' translates en hemin (lit. 'in us').
notes.4:10: The Greek hilasmos ('propitiation') refers to an atoning sacrifice that removes sin and turns away divine wrath.
notes.4:19: The earliest Greek manuscripts read simply 'We love' without a direct object; later manuscripts add 'Him'.
notes.5:6: The phrase 'water and blood' is widely understood to refer to Jesus' baptism and sacrificial death on the cross.
notes.5:7: The earliest and best Greek manuscripts omit the later Latin expansion known as the Comma Johanneum (which mentions three heavenly witnesses: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit).
notes.5:16: The 'sin leading to death' is often understood as willful, persistent apostasy or rejection of Christ; the implied subject of 'will give' is commonly taken to be God, though some understand the praying believer as God's instrument.
notes.5:18: The shift from the perfect participle ('everyone who has been born of God') to the aorist participle ('the One who was born of God') with the object 'him' (auton) in the earliest manuscripts points to Christ guarding the believer; later manuscripts read 'keeps himself' (heauton).
notes.5:20: Grammatically, 'This One' (houtos) can refer either to the nearest antecedent, Jesus Christ, or back to 'the True One' (God the Father); many interpreters see an intentional affirmation of Christ's full deity.
